cases.original_forecast: A salt-induced activity-coefficient change can shift the predicted cell voltage even with unchanged analytical copper and zinc amounts.

criteria.criterion: Compare the voltage change with the actual solved free-ion activities.
Do not prescribe a shift direction without those activities.

limitations: Actual activity/speciation and temperatures determine the shift. No prescribed sign from analytical concentration alone; slow Zn-water limit is unrelated to nonconsuming potential readback.

cases.original_forecast: Cumulative copper metal deposition cannot substantially exceed the 0.5 mmol zinc electron-donor budget; later copper additions increasingly remain dissolved.

criteria.criterion: Sum zinc oxidation and copper reduction across all doses.
Residual Cu2+ after the final dose is not misreported as a lack of initial reaction.

limitations: Finite donor exhaustion, not a complete kinetic or corrosion claim. Named initial Zn-water dissolution/rate limits do not negate later independently accounted Cu displacement.

cases.original_forecast: The mixed acetate/phosphate sample should retain an additional buffering region after the acetate-only sample approaches exhaustion.

criteria.criterion: Identify buffering intervals from incremental pH changes, not from an assumed common starting pH.
Account separately for all phosphate proton-equivalent steps and for acetate.

limitations: Compare incremental pH spans against each own starting pH and actual temperatures; separate phosphate proton equivalents and acetate, without assuming equal total formal buffer capacities.

cases.original_forecast: Sulfate should strongly compete for barium. Only after sufficient barium is available can substantial carbonate precipitation coexist; neither anion may consume the same barium twice.

criteria.criterion: Sum barium in every solid and aqueous species against its input.
Compare phase allocation in the barium-deficient and barium-excess-to-sulfate arms.

limitations: Sulfate allocation is real, but missing Witherite/BaCO3 excludes the competing carbonate phase required by the original question. Barium closure does not make unsupported carbonate chemistry pass.

cases.original_forecast: The acetate-buffered arm spends hydroxide on its acid reserve, delaying extensive copper hydroxide precipitation compared with the unbuffered arm.

criteria.criterion: Separate base spent on acetate protonation from the formal 2 OH per Cu precipitation budget.
Later base addition should change pH and phase allocation, not create extra copper.

limitations: Metastable supported hydroxide/basic-sulfate domain only. Explicit Tenorite formation-temperature exclusion is retained, not a claim of full oxide nucleation/phase equilibrium. Acid/acetate and all other Cu solids stay accounted.

cases.original_forecast: A calcium-phosphate-bearing solid may capture phosphorus from solution; acidification of the isolated solid should favour dissolved phosphate species.

criteria.criterion: Identify the actual calcium phosphate phase and track total phosphorus through filtration.
Dissolution must release phosphorus from the retained solid, not merely change liquid pH.

limitations: Actual octacalcium-phosphate capture and acid remobilisation only. Withheld Hydroxylapatite/beta-Ca3(PO4)2 metastability remains explicit; no automatic crystalline-equilibrium/nucleation claim.

cases.original_forecast: The activated arm should generate titratable acetic acid in proportion to ethanol converted. The unactivated arm tests whether an explicit named reaction is required.

criteria.criterion: Relate the blank-corrected base demand to the observed ethanol loss and acetate-family gain.
Account for any oxygen initially present in the sealed headspace instead of equating explicit oxygen addition with the entire oxygen budget.

limitations: Requested stoichiometric oxidation template, not spontaneous mechanism or calibrated rate. Initial air oxygen, carbonic acidity, endpoint protonation and reagent water remain separately accounted.

cases.original_forecast: The requested respiration can release up to 0.0006 mol of carbon dioxide from this glucose dose. Lime addition may transfer some of that carbon into carbonate solid while the rest remains in dissolved or gaseous pools.

criteria.criterion: Account for all six carbons per converted glucose across every retained carbon-bearing pool.
Identify carbonate separately from any excess unreacted calcium hydroxide before using retained solid mass as a carbon assay.

limitations: Glucose/carbonate questions have positive partial evidence, but original closed N/O and possibly traceC budgets fail when historical filter silently drops headspace. Later accepted gas-preserving filter may address; no new current-source failure claimed.

cases.original_forecast: A temperature-dependent transport model can change conductivity during warming even though sodium and chloride totals are unchanged. Cooling tests reversibility rather than chemical consumption.

criteria.criterion: Verify constant retained salt totals and inspect any water loss or volume change.
Identify whether the instrument reports temperature-compensated or in-situ conductivity before interpreting the sign and magnitude.

metrics.source_basis: 25C limiting ionic mobilities plus concentration correction; no explicit temperature transport argument.
metrics.volume_instrument_limit: Original volume_meter on open vessel refused; independent retained water and scene layers provide ownership control, not a fabricated instrument reading.

limitations: Small conductivity changes alone do not establish in-situ temperature-dependent transport or actual temperature compensation. Source reference table and measured temperatures expose the missing authority; original physical-temperature experiment is held.

cases.original_forecast: Warm water first supplies sensible and latent energy to the cold portion. The final temperature should fall below a liquid-only weighted-temperature prediction when initial ice is present.

criteria.criterion: Read the actual initial ice fraction and temperature before estimating a fusion energy.
Close the energy balance including warming any sub-zero solid and the measured final liquid.

limitations: Pure-water phase-specific sensible/latent balance; actual starting ice fraction at273.15K, so no subzero solid warming is omitted. No empirical calorimeter calibration.

cases.original_forecast: When supported by the coupled brine/ice model, salt lowers the freezing equilibrium temperature and promotes melting that consumes latent energy. Cooling and melting can therefore occur together.

criteria.criterion: Compare both temperature and ice fraction before and after salt addition.
Include salt dissolution energy and any undissolved salt in the interpretation, rather than attributing every joule to freezing-point depression.

limitations: Include actual salt dissolution and all ice/liquid enthalpy, not cooling/melting signs alone. Historical phase-energy failure, if present, is not automatically a current-source defect.
